# Mindwtr

> Official product and documentation links for Mindwtr, a free, open-source, local-first GTD and to-do app.

Mindwtr works offline, requires no account, and keeps primary task data on the user's device. Optional sync is user-controlled. The application is licensed under AGPL-3.0 and is available for desktop, mobile, and web.

## Product

- [Mindwtr home](https://mindwtr.app/): Product summary, screenshots, platform downloads, and comparison table.
- [Features](https://mindwtr.app/features): GTD workflow, views, sync, automation, integrations, and supported platforms.
- [Comparison](https://mindwtr.app/compare): Full sourced matrix — Mindwtr vs Todoist, TickTick, Everdo, Nirvana, OmniFocus, Things 3, and Microsoft To Do — plus scope boundaries and FAQ.
- [What is GTD?](https://mindwtr.app/gtd): Plain-language introduction to Getting Things Done and its five-step workflow.
- [Guides](https://mindwtr.app/guides): Index of every method guide, psychology article, and app comparison on the site.
- [Mindwtr Handbook](https://mindwtr.app/handbook): Narrative overview of running a complete GTD system in Mindwtr, linking into the documentation.
- [Support](https://mindwtr.app/support): Help routes, bug reporting, feature requests, and community links.
- [Privacy policy](https://mindwtr.app/privacy): Data handling for the website and applications.
- [Brand and trademark](https://mindwtr.app/brand): Official name, logo, and trademark guidance.

## Comparisons

- [Todoist alternative](https://mindwtr.app/todoist-alternative): Mindwtr vs Todoist — sourced head-to-head table, honest trade-offs, and the Todoist import path.
- [TickTick alternative](https://mindwtr.app/ticktick-alternative): Mindwtr vs TickTick — free-plan limits, offline and account differences, and the TickTick import path.
- [Everdo alternative](https://mindwtr.app/everdo-alternative): Mindwtr vs Everdo — two local-first GTD apps compared on license, price, and sync; CSV migration route.
- [OmniFocus for Linux](https://mindwtr.app/omnifocus-for-linux): OmniFocus is Apple-only; Mindwtr on Linux, Windows, and Android, with a first-class OmniFocus importer.
- [Free GTD app for Android](https://mindwtr.app/free-gtd-app-android): Mindwtr on Android vs Todoist and TickTick — Google Play, F-Droid, widgets, offline, no account.
- [Todoist alternatives](https://mindwtr.app/todoist-alternatives): Roundup of Todoist alternatives profiled honestly — strengths, catches, pricing, and who each app fits.
- [TickTick alternatives](https://mindwtr.app/ticktick-alternatives): Roundup of TickTick alternatives profiled honestly — strengths, catches, pricing, and who each app fits.
- [Best free task manager](https://mindwtr.app/best-free-task-manager): What "free" actually means — free tiers, free products, and free software — across eight task managers.

## Method guides

- [Psychology of GTD](https://mindwtr.app/gtd-psychology): Why GTD works — open loops, working memory limits, external thinking, and review, with sourced citations.
- [Zeigarnik effect](https://mindwtr.app/zeigarnik-effect): The interrupted-task effect, its mixed replication record, and the plan-making finding GTD builds on.
- [Cognitive overload](https://mindwtr.app/cognitive-overload): Working memory capacity, cognitive load, attention residue, and how GTD reduces mental load.
- [Distributed cognition](https://mindwtr.app/distributed-cognition): Thinking with external artifacts — Hutchins, the extended mind, and the requirements of a trusted system.
- [GTD horizons of focus](https://mindwtr.app/gtd-horizons): The six horizons from next actions to purpose, and a review-based practice for goals and visions.
- [Task apps and ADHD](https://mindwtr.app/adhd): What makes a task system survivable when attention and working memory are unreliable; not medical advice.
- [Common GTD problems](https://mindwtr.app/gtd-problems): The walls long-term GTD practitioners hit — stalled reviews, bloated lists, dead contexts — and the method-level fixes.
